title: Dell Precision 7680 Common Issues & Fixes
content:
### Frequent symptoms
- Coil whine or fan surge under light loads when Dell Optimizer power profiles are disabled.
- Thermal throttling during CAD/render workloads caused by dust-packed fin stacks.
- USB4/TB4 docks intermittently dropping displays after sleep.

### Troubleshooting workflow
1. Update BIOS to 1.16.0+ and Intel ME firmware from Dell Command Update.
2. Run SupportAssist hardware scans; escalate if thermals exceed 95°C sustained.
3. For docking instability, install the latest Intel graphics and Thunderbolt controller drivers, then reset the dock’s firmware by unplugging power for 30 seconds.
4. Re-seat SO-DIMMs if SupportAssist memory diagnostics fail, then rerun ePSA.

### Dell ePSA / SupportAssist error codes
- 2000-0123 – Memory integrity failure. Steps: test each DIMM in slot A only; replace the failing module.
- 2000-0141 – No hard drive detected. Steps: verify NVMe seating, toggle RAID/ACHI in BIOS, and replace SSD if absent in BIOS.
- 2000-0151 – CPU fan failure. Steps: clear dust, inspect fan cable, replace heatsink assembly if RPM remains 0.
- 2000-0511 – GPU fan failure. Steps: same as CPU fan; document temps for Dell escalation.

### Escalation notes
- Capture thermal logs from SupportAssist and HWinfo64.
- Provide dock model, cable length, and external monitor specs for graphics-related tickets.
- Include BIOS export (F12 setup) and service tag in the escalation email.

title: Dell Precision 7670 – Known Field Issues
content:
### Frequent symptoms
- Battery swelling or chassis lift near the clickpad after 18+ months of heavy charge cycles.
- Intermittent keyboard backlight outages tied to BIOS 1.9.x.
- NVMe throttling when the bottom cover vents are obstructed by desk mats.

### Troubleshooting workflow
1. Inspect battery physically; if swollen, disconnect power immediately and replace the pack.
2. Update BIOS to 1.14.x or newer and reset EC via 30-second power drain.
3. Reflash keyboard firmware through Dell Peripheral Manager when backlight zones fail.
4. For storage throttling, reseat NVMe with new thermal pad and run ePSA drive tests.

### Common error codes
- 2000-0161 – RTC power failure. Steps: replace coin-cell battery and reset BIOS defaults.
- 2000-0155 – Thermal sensor failure. Steps: verify fan harness, update BIOS, replace heatsink assembly if code persists.
- 2000-0142 – Drive self-test cannot be completed. Steps: clone critical data, secure erase, replace SSD if SMART fails.

### Escalation checklist
- Attach thermal screenshots and battery photos.
- Provide SupportAssist log bundle (.zip) and AC adapter wattage.
- Confirm part availability before authorizing onsite service.

title: Dell Precision 7580 / 7570 Support Playbook
content:
### Frequent symptoms
- POST hang at Dell logo when discrete GPU is enabled.
- Fan cycling loudly at idle because of Dell Optimizer performance profiles.
- USB 3.1 ports dropping power to scanners/printers during remote sessions.

### Troubleshooting workflow
1. Update BIOS and GPU firmware; if POST hang persists, toggle switchable graphics off, boot, then re-enable after driver refresh.
2. Run Dell Optimizer, select Quiet mode, and update Intel Dynamic Platform & Thermal Framework drivers.
3. Disable USB selective suspend in Windows power plan and update chipset drivers.
4. Reset SupportAssist OS Recovery partition when Windows repair loops are reported.

### Error codes to track
- 2000-0131 – CPU cache failure. Steps: reseat CPU (for serviceable units) or escalate for motherboard replacement.
- 2000-0415 – USB controller failure. Steps: test bare-bones boot, reseat daughterboard, replace system board if persistent.
- 2000-0712 – Alert! TPM self-test failure. Steps: clear TPM in BIOS, update firmware, replace system board if the error remains.

### Escalation checklist
- Include GPU model, driver versions, and dock/peripheral list.
- Document BIOS revision and whether legacy/UEFI boot is enabled.
- Attach SupportAssist hardware test screenshots.

title: All Dell PCs – High-Frequency Error Codes & First Response
content:
### Top SupportAssist / ePSA codes
- 2000-0111 – CPU fan failure. Steps: reseat fan cable, check fan spin in BIOS diagnostics, replace fan.
- 2000-0123 – Memory integrity failure. Steps: test modules individually, swap slots, replace module or motherboard.
- 2000-0141 – No hard drive detected. Steps: reseat storage, update BIOS/SATA mode, replace drive if absent in BIOS.
- 2000-0142 – Drive self-test cannot be completed. Steps: back up data, run OEM drive firmware update, replace drive if SMART fails.
- 2000-0151 – CPU temperature sensor failure. Steps: clean heatsink, refresh thermal paste, replace thermal assembly.
- 2000-0152 – System board failure. Steps: disconnect non-essential devices, perform BIOS recovery, escalate for board swap.
- 2000-0162 – Battery temperature error. Steps: inspect battery, update BIOS, replace battery if swollen or failing.
- 2000-0165 – AC adapter wattage cannot be determined. Steps: test with known-good adapter, inspect DC-in jack, update BIOS.
- 2000-0170 – Hard drive error detected. Steps: reseat or replace drive after cloning data.
- 2000-0511 – GPU fan failure. Steps: inspect GPU fan cable, clean vents, replace GPU heatsink/fan module.

### Universal intake questions
1. Confirm service tag, OS build, BIOS version, and dock/peripherals.
2. Ask about recent changes (Windows updates, driver installs, hardware additions).
3. Check SupportAssist history for recent failed updates or repairs.
4. Gather event viewer critical logs and minidumps for blue-screen cases.

### First-response checklist
- Run F12 diagnostics (ePSA) and capture the reference number.
- Update BIOS, chipset, storage, and graphics through Dell Command Update.
- Verify Windows power/battery reports with `powercfg /batteryreport`.
- Document any third-party encryption or security software before OS repair.
- For thermal complaints, photograph vent obstructions and log fan RPM/temps.

### Escalation package
- ePSA reference, SupportAssist log bundle, system inventory export, photos/videos.
- Steps already attempted, OS rebuild status, and warranty coverage confirmation.
- Customer impact assessment and requested next action (onsite, depot, parts).

title: 3Shape TRIOS 3/4/5/6 Scanner Troubleshooting Knowledge Base
content:
### Hardware & Connectivity Differences
- **TRIOS 3** uses USB-A 3.0 with an external power pod; firmware below 1.4.9 is prone to USB selective suspend dropouts on Windows 10 21H1. Disable USB power saving on hubs and update to the latest Unite-certified firmware before replacing cables.
- **TRIOS 4** adds built-in battery and Wi-Fi for pod-less operation. Frequent disconnects usually trace back to depleted smart batteries (<15%) or outdated Wi-Fi dongle firmware. Cycle the batteries monthly and keep pod firmware at 1.6.x to stabilize sleep recovery.
- **TRIOS 5** introduces a pen grip with LED scanner status ring and wireless charging puck. Most wake failures are caused by clogged contact pads—clean with 70% IPA and reseat the puck. Replace the magnetic cable if LED stays amber after 30 minutes on charge.
- **TRIOS 6** ships with USB-C hardwiring and new field-replaceable tips with thermal sensors. USB-C cables longer than 2 m cause enumeration failures; stick to the 1.8 m shielded cable bundled by 3Shape.

### Calibration & Optics
- **Shared drift symptoms**: washed-out surfaces, double contours, or occlusion holes. Always verify the tip glass is seated and cool (below 40 °C). Run Unite → Settings → Scanners → Calibrate; expect green checks within 3–5 minutes.
- **TRIOS 3/4** rely on the black/white calibration tile. If the tile is warped or matte finish is worn, scans skew 50–100 µm; replace the tile yearly.
- **TRIOS 5/6** use the Sphere Calibration unit. Error 1060 typically indicates the sphere QR code is unreadable—clean the window and re-register the accessory under Scanner Tools.
- If the scanner rejects calibration with error 3112/3113, confirm that the Unite PC regional format uses a dot decimal separator; commas interfere with calibration data parsing in firmware <1.5.2.

### Thermal & Fan Alerts
- **TRIOS 3** internal fans clog easily in dusty labs. Unite logs will show warning 20102 (over-temperature). Blow compressed air through the vent slots and check fan RPM via TRIOS Diagnostic Tool. Persisting warnings require fan module swap.
- **TRIOS 4** triggers Battery Overheat warnings if scanning continuously on Wi-Fi dock; switch to pod power for long cases and update firmware to leverage the revised thermal curve introduced in 2022 Q4.
- **TRIOS 5/6** log Code 47 when tip thermistor exceeds 48 °C. Cooling the tip under running water (never submerge handle) for 30 seconds resolves most cases. Document ambient room temps >28 °C for escalation.

### Image Quality & Color Issues
- **Grainy or color-shifted scans** often come from smudged mirrors. Use lint-free swabs with 70% IPA; never use acetone on TRIOS 5/6 sapphire windows.
- Firmware 1.7.x introduced HDR color capture; ensure Unite 23.2 or later is installed. For older PCs, disable HDR in Unite → Settings if GPU is Intel UHD 620 or lower to prevent stuttering.
- For **TRIOS 3** units showing banding, verify the USB pod firmware matches the scanner firmware. Mixed firmware levels lead to exposure desync (Support FAQ ID 1157).

### Wireless & Battery Checks (TRIOS 4/5/6)
- Use 3Shape Battery Tool to read cycle counts. Replace packs once capacity falls below 80% to avoid sudden shutdowns mid-scan.
- Wi-Fi dropouts while using Move+ carts commonly stem from DFS channel interference. Configure the access point to fixed channel 36/40 and keep the scanner within 5 m line-of-sight.
- LED sequence reference: solid green = ready, pulsing blue = pairing, flashing red = thermal fault, pulsing amber = low battery.

### Software & Licensing
- Unite must be 22.1+ for TRIOS 5/6 recognition. If scanners are absent, remove residual USB drivers (`Device Manager → View hidden devices → Universal Serial Bus devices`) and reinstall Unite.
- License expiration warnings after RMA shipments occur when the faulty device is not checked in within 32 days. Confirm the RMA case in 3Shape eSupport shows "device received" before closing the ticket.
- When switching scanners between clinics, always de-register the device in Unite → Accounts; otherwise, calibration data remains locked to the previous site and prevents new logins.

### Escalation Triggers
- Collect logs via `C:\ProgramData\3Shape\Logs\TRIOS` and include the `*.tdslog` file.
- Record firmware, pod serial, tip serial, battery cycles, and Unite version.
- Provide photos of error messages and the physical condition of tips, calibration targets, and charging docks.
- Escalate immediately if the scanner emits burning odor, shows recurring Error 4110 (laser fault), or fails LED self-test on boot.

title: Windows Runtime & Stability Troubleshooting Playbook
content:
### .NET runtime repair and install
- **Identify the target version**: run `dotnet --info` for SDK/runtime builds or check **Programs and Features → Microsoft .NET** entries. Use `reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\NET Framework Setup\NDP" /s` when GUI access is limited.
- **Common setup blockers**: error 0x800F081F or 0x80072F8F indicates missing CBS payloads; run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` followed by `sfc /scannow`, then rerun the offline installer for the specific runtime (Desktop vs Hosting vs ASP.NET).
- **Repair existing installs**: `dotnet-runtime-<version>-win-x64.exe /repair` or, for legacy .NET Framework 4.x, use the official `ndp48-x86-x64-allos-enu.exe /repair`. Capture `%temp%` log folders (e.g., `dd_dotnetfx*.log`) before closing the wizard.
- **Uninstall/reinstall**: when components are corrupted beyond repair, remove the target build with **Apps & Features** or the .NET Cleanup Tool, reboot, and install fresh from the offline package. Document whether the machine is offline or locked down for firewall approvals.

### Microsoft Visual C++ redistributable failures
- **Symptoms**: application launches raise `MSVCP140.dll`/`VCRUNTIME140.dll` missing, `api-ms-win-crt-runtime-l1-1-0.dll` errors, or setup logs show `Error 1935`.
- **Baseline actions**: confirm both x86 and x64 redistributables are installed for the release year the app targets (2012, 2013, 2015-2022 bundle). Use `winget list Microsoft.VC++` or inspect `Programs and Features`.
- **Repair flow**: download the latest vc_redist packages from Microsoft, run with `/repair`, then reinstall with `/install /quiet /norestart` if scripted deployment is needed. For Error 1935, re-enable the Windows Modules Installer service and run `DISM`/`SFC` before retrying.
- **Cleanup**: remove stale prerelease builds, reboot, and reinstall. Capture `%windir%\Logs\CBS\CBS.log` and `dd_vcredist*.log` for escalation if failures persist.

### Application install/uninstall blockers
- **Installation**: enable verbose MSI logging via `msiexec /i setup.msi /L*V %temp%\app_install.log`. Check for pending reboots (`reg query HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager /v PendingFileRenameOperations`). Use the **Program Install and Uninstall** troubleshooter when Windows Installer metadata is corrupt.
- **Uninstallation**: run `msiexec /x {PRODUCT-CODE} /L*V %temp%\app_uninstall.log`, clear remnants under `%ProgramData%`, `%ProgramFiles%`, and `%AppData%`. For stubborn cases, boot Safe Mode, remove services with `sc delete`, and clean driver packages via `pnputil /enum-drivers`.
- **Deployment tips**: verify disk space and AV exclusions, disable third-party endpoint protection temporarily, and confirm the user context has local admin rights.

### Crash and bluescreen triage
- **Immediate capture**: collect the bugcheck code/parameters from Event Viewer (`System` log, source *BugCheck*), grab `%SystemRoot%\MEMORY.DMP` or `%SystemRoot%\Minidump`. Note recent driver or Windows updates.
- **Rapid health checks**: run `sfc /scannow`, `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth`, and `chkdsk /scan`. Use `wmic qfe list brief` to identify recent patches to roll back. For suspected driver issues, run `verifier /querysettings` and disable Driver Verifier if active.
- **Analysis**: open minidumps in WinDbg (`!analyze -v`) to identify the faulting module. Hardware suspects (0x124, 0x9C) require Dell/Lenovo diagnostics; memory errors warrant `mdsched.exe` or MemTest86 overnight.
- **Escalation package**: include dump files, `systeminfo` output, list of connected peripherals, and any overclocking or third-party driver utilities in use.

### Documentation & customer communication
- Record whether the machine belongs to production or lab, note maintenance windows, and confirm backups before registry edits.
- Provide remediation status (repaired, pending reboot, escalated) and next follow-up time when handing off to 2nd line or engineering.

title: Kiroshi AI Deep Knowledge Pack – Field Diagnostics
content:
### GPU performance & thermals
- **NVIDIA driver resets (TDR)**: capture `Display driver nvlddmkm stopped responding` events; raise TDR delay via `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\GraphicsDrivers` → `TdrDelay=10`. Run `sfc`/`DISM`, then clean-install current Studio or OEM driver with `nvidia-smi --query`.
- **Heaven benchmark baselines**: run Unigine Heaven 4.0 in windowed 1920×1080, High preset, 4×AA. Document FPS, temps, and fan ramp. >90 °C on Dell mobile workstations signals clogged fins; export logs to correlate with SupportAssist thermal data.
- **Overheating playbook**: inspect vents, reseat heatsink, replace thermal paste (Arctic MX-6), ensure Dell Optimizer quiet modes disabled, verify BIOS thermal tables. Capture HWinfo sensors before/after cleaning.
- **Intel Ultra & Iris Xe tuning**: update Intel Graphics Command Center profile, disable panel self refresh, check Intel Dynamic Tuning Technology status. Apply latest chipset + ME firmware from Dell Command Update.

### Dell Precision & workstation escalations
- Maintain matrix of BIOS/firmware for Precision 35x0/55x0/75x0; document VRAM throttling cases with HWinfo logs.
- For random shutdowns, disable C-states temporarily, reseat RAM, and run ePSA extended. Note service tag, dock model, PSU wattage, and CPU package power when creating Dell escalation blocks.

### 3Shape Unite, Help Center & community intelligence
- **Core flows**: verify Unite version under *Settings → About*, sync apps via `UniteLauncher.exe --repair`, and clear `%LocalAppData%\3Shape\DentalDesktopCache`.
- **Knowledge mining**: tag articles for TRIOS tips, Unite login failures, export/print queues, and DTX Studio Bridge steps.
- **Forum watchlist**: log recurring posts on driver 2.0.3 misreads, TRIOS calibration loops, and Unite cloud outages; map them to internal KB IDs.

### Dentistry & implant refresher
- Maintain glossary for crown, bridge, abutment, margin line, edentulous, osteotomy, torque spec.
- Implant workflow: CBCT planning → guide fabrication → scan body capture → final restoration; note common chairside blockers (scan bodies swapped, insufficient retraction).

### Data platforms & runtimes
- **MSSQL**: typical Unite/OrthoAnalyzer DB path `C:\ProgramData\3Shape\Data\Database`. Use `sqlcmd -S .\TRIOS -Q "SELECT @@VERSION"`. Check SQL Browser/Agent services, shrink log with `DBCC SHRINKFILE`, repair with `DBCC CHECKDB (TRIOS) WITH REPAIR_ALLOW_DATA_LOSS` only after full backup.
- **Visual C++**: ensure 2015-2022 redistributable (x86 + x64) installed; leverage repair switches when Unite or scanner services fail to start.

### TRIOS scanner family quick hits
- **TRIOS 4**: log battery health (TRIOS Tray), inspect tip counter, firmware 2.5.2+, clean mirror; document calibration and community sentiment.
- **TRIOS 3**: verify USB 3.0 powered hub, update scanner service pack, run legacy calibration tile.
- **TRIOS 5/6**: capture Unite health indicator, ensure Wi-Fi 6E profiles stable, run antimicrobial sleeve alignment guide.

### Windows servicing & recovery
- Patch cadence: record KB IDs, use `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /ScanHealth`, defer feature updates on scanners.
- Reflash/repair: create USB via `MediaCreationTool`, boot to WinRE, run `setup.exe /repair /quiet`. For bare metal, backup `%ProgramData%\3Shape`, export SQL DB, reinstall Windows, then restore backups + licensing.

### Networking & connectivity
- Scanner networking: static IP for cart, disable power saving on NIC, verify ports 443/5000, run `triosnetworktool.exe`.
- General troubleshooting: map topology, run `pathping`, capture Wireshark traces, segment VLAN QoS, validate DNS split-brain scenarios.
- TP-Link switches/APs: update firmware, disable Smart Connect when scanners drop, lock channel width to 40 MHz.
- Intel Ethernet/Killer suites: uninstall Killer Intelligence Center, install Intel PROSet driver-only package; disable EEE/Power Management causing throughput drops.

### Knowledge tags for AI assistance
- Associate each bullet with keywords (nvidia, heaven, overheating, intel ultra, dell precision, unite, forum, dentistry, implant, mssql, trios, windows update, reimage, networking, tplink, killer).
- Encourage agents to add case IDs referencing these notes so AI Educate classification surfaces deep history.

title: Case AI Assistance – QA Framework (3Shape Support)
content:
### Scope and weightings
- CX quality focus: Call Control 10%, Soft Skills 40%, Communication 20%, Closure 30%.

### Call Control (Opening, Hold/Mute, Transfer)
- Opening: mention 3Shape, introduce yourself, offer help; collect or confirm name and phone (email not required in chat); do this before troubleshooting unless it is reseller/IT/transfer-only.
- Hold/Mute: explain reason and expected duration; refresh the interaction before 5 minutes on chat/hold (2 minutes for mute, 30 seconds for dead air); give updates and thank for patience.
- Transfer: move the user to the correct team within 3 minutes; avoid repeated steps, share background and needed info to reduce user effort.

### Soft Skills
- Keep a positive, respectful, professional tone with steady rhythm; show willingness to assist and empathy/apology where appropriate.
- Display ownership by spotting ways to reduce user effort and improve experience within role scope.

### Communication
- Written communication: send emails to involved people with issue/request, root cause, prevention/fix guidance, recommendations, and survey script (recap must include those items).
- Clear communication: ask purposeful questions, paraphrase, and keep a clear path to identify the issue.

### Closure
- Resolution & expectations: provide correct resolution aligned to guidelines; address root cause/core request and set clear next steps and time frames.
- Recap: short summary with troubleshooting performed and final resolution; offer extra help once.
- Closing: proactively give the Case ID, explain its value for follow-up, and mention the survey (no survey on open cases).
- Follow up: perform within required timelines; complete documentation/emails before closing the case.

### Call/Case Procedures (CP)
- Background: proactively check/document whether any interaction or case exists in the last month for the same issue; include replacement history for DSO.
- Troubleshooting: follow precise, documented steps using available resources—reproduce, research, execute, and test before giving resolution.
- Root causing: leverage tools and research to identify the driver of the issue/request.

### Notes
- General notes: include all necessary case notes (call/chat/email), internal notes, escalations, and HelpJuice link; capture names (end user/reseller), paraphrased issue, callback number; record end-user contact unless it is a new user who never communicated.
- Customer details: verify and fill missing contact info in the CRM contact card.
- Remote session (Reseller/IT only): in the remote session note, list precise steps/actions on the user equipment plus evidence (screenshots, videos, logs, photos) without repeating past troubleshooting; may stay as an internal note.

### CRM Documentation
- Description tab: capture what/where/when for the request/complaint, including EMs/warnings/pop-ups; add logs, screenshots, and numeric software version (for requests only what/where).
- Additional info: add accurate gathered details that aid understanding and highlight possible root causes; include general product info for NTC requests.
- Identification tab: fill Title as "Ticket from Straumann (2nd)/Practice Name/SID/brief request or complaint (EMs/pop-ups/warnings)"; mark Special Attention/Reportable; set Product family/product/sub-product, origin (phone/chat/email), and priority (normal/serious/critical); use D# instead of SID for labs; attach logs/screenshots/software version.
- Numbers tab: enter SID, software version, and all other related numbers tied to the selected product; include logs/screenshots/software version (SV not needed if no remote access).
- Categorization tab: set category, area, and type aligned with the root cause.
- Conclusion: make root cause clear and base it on the decision-making process; resolution must explain how it was resolved.
- Disposition: set the Five9 disposition.

### Service notes
- For chat interactions, the same quality expectations apply to timing, clarity, recap, and documentation steps above.

### QA simulation (when AI Assistance is checked)
- Add a realistic, single QA note summarizing how the interaction met Call Control, Soft Skills, Communication, Closure, CP, Notes, CRM documentation, and Service notes; call out any gaps and next actions.
- Example QA note: "QA SIM: Opening used 3Shape intro, confirmed name/phone; provided mute notice every 2 min; no transfer. Empathy shown for scanner downtime; questions paraphrased. Recap shared steps (updated TRIOS software, reseated pod), set expectation to call back with logs in 24h, provided Case ID and survey info. CRM: Description/Identification/Numbers tabs completed with SID 12345 and SW 24.3. Notes include HJ link and remote actions. Follow-up scheduled tomorrow."
